answer: Randomness-anchored ticket window. Each new identity draws a slot from a public beacon whose seed is fixed only after registration closes, so an attacker cannot wander through candidate seeds to pick favorable ones. Registration requires holding a ticket whose validity depends on that unseen draw, meaning any clone batch must be committed before learning which tickets survive, and failures are sunk with no refund. A comet of late-arriving identities cannot retry cheaply because each attempt costs one full ticket plus the expected loss from the hollow odds of matching the revealed window.
